as_told.title: PEER project trains abductees to question their abductors

plain: Around 2004 at Harvard, a Harvard professor named John Mack and a lawyer named Dan Sheehan set out to train people who said they were taken by aliens again and again, so they could handle those meetings better. Sheehan tells it as someone who took part. He says he was legal counsel to Mack's group, the Program for Extraordinary Experience Research, and that the plan used holotropic breathing, a fast, deep breathing method meant to bring on altered states. In another telling he leaves out the breathing and stresses teaching these people to question the beings who took them, which would mean treating the encounters as real conversations.
